IncidentBot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT DETECTED - spike in 5xx + degraded outputs for /v1/chat across EU regions. Alert threshold crossed (5m error rate > 8%). Paging oncall: @Ben (oncall).

Ben (oncall): seeing it. I'm pulling traces. Initial hypothesis: routing policy is falling back to a quantized variant that doesn't support function/tool-calling, causing downstream errors when customers send `tool_call` payloads.

Maya (ml-eng): that matches a couple of failed requests I scanned — responses are truncated or JSON-invalid when `tool_call` is present. Quantized variant was recently added to the variant catalog for cost optimization.

Priya (support): Customer-reported: "chat responses became gibberish and calls that used our tool hooks started 500ing" — major customer in EU. Ticket INC-5423 opened.

Ben (oncall): timeline: around 17:58 UTC routing policy `cost_prefer_quant` started hitting EU pools. Looks like smart-routing selected `gptx-quant-8bit` instead of `gptx-fp16` when `tool_call`=true — that's a mismatch.

Carlos (prod): Did the policy change rollout yesterday? We had a canary for `cost_prefer_quant` last night.

Maya (ml-eng): yes, but the compatibility matrix we use for routing didn't mark `gptx-quant-8bit` as "no-tool-call" — bug in onboarding script. The policy logic only checks `model_variant in allowed_variants` and then separately evaluates `capabilities`, but the capabilities lookup failed due to a missing key for `gptx-quant-8bit`.

Ben (oncall): immediate mitigation: disabling smart-routing for affected customer routes and forcing `model_variant=gptx-fp16` for their API key. Doing now.

IncidentBot: Deploybot: routing policy change: `cost_prefer_quant` rollout paused (change id: rpl-8903).

Ben (oncall): applied temporary per-customer override via Console -> Customers -> customer-123 -> "Pinned model" = `gptx-fp16`. Monitoring.

Maya (ml-eng): quick note — quantized variant also has a shorter context limit (8k vs 32k). Some calls with long contexts were leading to truncation errors that the client interprets as malformed output. Compatibility matrix snippet I pulled from onboarding logs:

```
model_variant, supports_tool_call, max_context_tokens
gptx-fp16, true, 32768
gptx-quant-8bit, false, 8192
gptx-int4, false, 4096
```

Maya (ml-eng): we never wrote a guard that prohibits `cost_prefer_quant` from being selected when `tool_call` is requested. That's the root cause.

Priya (support): Customer confirmed improved responses after pin to fp16. They reported latency was slightly higher but correctness restored.

Ben (oncall): mitigation status: overrides in place for the five most impacted customers; smart-routing paused globally for EU->quantized pool. Error rate dropped to baseline in ~3m.

Carlos (prod): next steps: 1) patch routing service to consult capabilities map atomically, 2) add unit tests for tool_call compatibility, 3) update canary gating so that variants without full capability labels can't be included in `cost_prefer_quant` rollouts.

Maya (ml-eng): I'm taking (1) and (2). Will open PR with tests and a migration to re-evaluate the entire variant catalog on startup.

Ben (oncall): I'll do the customer comms template and note the temporary override. Priya can you send the incident update to the affected accounts?

Priya (support): On it. Draft: "We temporarily pinned your model to gptx-fp16 to restore tool-calling reliability. We're investigating a routing configuration regression that selected a quantized variant lacking tool-calling support. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline."

Carlos (prod): Also we saw a region fallback loop: when quantized pool rejected requests due to unsupported payload, the router retried against another region which also had the quantized variant, and TTL-based fallback kept cycling between EU zones for ~40s. Need to add a fast-fail when capability mismatch is detected to avoid cross-region loops.

Maya (ml-eng): good catch. I'll add a capability-check early path in the router before any retry/fallback decision.

Ben (oncall): Handoff to Ravi for full incident until resolved. Ravi, summary: root cause = compatibility matrix missing capability entry for `gptx-quant-8bit` -> routing policy allowed selection -> tool-calling requests ended up on incompatible variant -> resp errors + region fallback loops. Mitigations applied: pinned impacted customers to fp16, paused quant rollouts in EU, applied per-route override, monitoring shows error rate normalized.

Ravi: Taking over. I'll coordinate postmortem and severity classification. Initial severity: Sev2 (customer-impacting, partial outage for select customers). I'll schedule a 30-min bridge in 10 minutes to walk through timeline and assign owners.

IncidentBot: Note: oncall handoff performed by Ben (oncall) -> Ravi at 18:04 UTC.

Ravi: Owners assigned: Maya (ml-eng) root-cause fix + tests, Ben -> ops follow-up (improve router fast-fail), Carlos -> product/change-gating for rollouts, Priya -> customer comms + post-incident summary. I'll collect logs for the postmortem (routing decisions, compatibility lookup traces, and canary rollout logs).

Priya (support): Customer update sent. They acknowledged and asked for timeline for permanent fix. I'll coordinate with Maya + Carlos for ETA.

Ben (oncall): Closing immediate page: system stable, overrides remain until fix merged + validated in canary.

Ravi: Thanks team. Will run full RCA template and postmortem doc linking to this thread. If anyone has follow-ups, drop them here.
